key_insight: Deep tabular generators did not consistently outperform simple baselines on small clinical or subsampled tabular datasets, and their rankings were more stable than expected at low sample sizes.
engineering_relevance: For synthetic tabular data generation in healthcare and other small-data settings, simple methods may be more reliable than deep models, so benchmark choice and sample size should guide model selection.
method: Preregistered size-ladder benchmark from 200 to 20,000 training rows on 8 public datasets
Compared 7 generators: independent marginals, Gaussian copula, SMOTE, unconditional SMOTE, CTGAN, TVAE, and TabDDPM
Evaluated with fixed downstream classifiers using AUROC, across 20 tuning trials and 5 evaluation seeds
evidence_signal: Across 2,220 runs, no deep model beat the best trivial baseline by more than seed noise in 23 of 24 dataset-model pairs, and the best baseline won 40 of 49 dataset-size cells.
watch_item: The gap between top methods was often smaller than seed-to-seed variation, so single-run results can be misleading and small ranking differences should not be over-interpreted.
paper_title: Below what training size do deep tabular generators stop beating trivial baselines? A preregistered benchmark on a size ladder of clinical and standard datasets
